5	// shows three money values: the budget that was set (project-budget), how much has been INVOICED
6	// against the project (project-invoiced — the sum of that project's own invoices), and what is LEFT
7	// (project-remaining — budget minus invoiced).
8	//
9	// Asserts ONLY through the UI (data-testid). Data is arranged via resetAndSeed, which honours
10	// projects: { id, clientId, name, budget } alongside clients and invoices: { id, projectId, amount }.
11	// The budget is SET by seeding it (the honoured `budget` field is the Arrange for "set a budget");
12	// there is no dedicated set-budget form — unlike every other write in the app, the change introduces
13	// no *-submit anchor for a budget, so the budget is a value the panel DISPLAYS, and the only write
14	// flow exercised here is raising an invoice through the existing invoice form, which is what
15	// "invoiced against it" and "what is left" must then reflect.
16	//
17	// Money values are asserted EXACTLY with toHaveText in the app's money format — a dollar sign and two
18	// decimals, "$900.00" — per the "show money properly everywhere" change (see money-format.spec.ts).
19	// A non-whole amount (99.5 -> $99.50) proves cents are padded to two places on the derived values.
20	// All amounts stay below 1000 so no thousands separator is involved, and no value is a substring of
21	// another. This SHOULD FAIL before the change: the project detail page carries no budget panel today.
